children: Market breadth weakened sharply, with only 42.34% of S&P 500 (
) stocks trading above their 50-day moving average as of Sept. 8, according to data shared by Barchart.

The reading marked the weakest market breadth in five months, Barchart said in a post on X. The measure had fallen sharply from levels above 60% through much of July and early August, when it reached roughly 70% before reversing lower.
The chart showed the percentage of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day moving average falling from around 69% in mid-August to 42.34% by Sept. 8.
The latest reading was also down 4.57 percentage points, or 9.74%, on the day, according to the Barchart chart.
The deterioration suggested that the market's recent weakness had spread across a broader share of S&P 500 constituents, rather than being confined to a small group of stocks.

title: S&P 500 breadth tumbles as only 42% of stocks clear 50-day average
